title: Erdős Problem #241: Maximum Size of B₃ Sets
description: Let f(N) be the maximum size of A ⊆ {1,...,N} with all three-element sums distinct. Is f(N) ~ N^{1/3}? Bose–Chowla achieved N^{1/3}; Green's upper bound is ~1.519·N^{1/3}. OPEN ($100 prize).

meta.author: Erdős
meta.assumptions: 6 axioms: bose_chowla_lower_bound, green_upper_bound, bose_chowla_h2_resolved, and 3 more. See Lean source for complete statements.

overview.historicalContext: B₃ sets emerged from the study of Sidon sets (B₂ sets), initiated by Simon Sidon in the 1930s and developed by Erdős and Turán (1941). The natural generalization to B₃ sets—where all ordered triple sums are distinct—was studied by R.C. Bose and S. Chowla. In their landmark 1962 paper 'Theorems in the additive theory of numbers,' Bose and Chowla constructed explicit B₃ sets of size $(1+o(1))N^{1/3}$ using the multiplicative structure of finite fields $\mathbb{F}_{p^3}$, specifically exploiting the injectivity of the cubing map. This algebraic construction parallels Singer's (1938) perfect difference set method for Sidon sets. The upper bound remained at the trivial $O(N^{1/3})$ for decades until Ben Green's 2001 breakthrough 'The number of squares and $B_h[g]$ sets,' which refined the constant to $(7/2)^{1/3} \approx 1.519$ using additive energy techniques. The persistent gap between the constants 1 and 1.519 represents one of the central open problems in additive combinatorics. The problem carries a $100 prize from Erdős and appears as Problem C11 in Guy's 'Unsolved Problems in Number Theory.' It is closely related to questions in coding theory, where B₃ sets correspond to certain error-correcting codes.
overview.problemStatement: Is $f(N) \sim N^{1/3}$, where $f(N)$ is the maximum size of a $B_3$ subset of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$?
overview.text: Let f(N) be the maximum size of A ⊆ {1,...,N} with all three-element sums distinct. Is f(N) ~ N^{1/3}? Bose–Chowla achieved N^{1/3}; Green's upper bound is ~1.519·N^{1/3}. OPEN ($100 prize).
overview.proofStrategy: We define IsB3 (all ordered triple sums distinct) and maxB3Size as the extremal function. The conjecture ErdosProblem241 asserts $f(N)/N^{1/3} \to 1$, formalized as an $\varepsilon$-$N_0$ statement. We axiomatize both the Bose–Chowla lower bound and Green's upper bound. The formalization extends to generalized $B_h$ sets with the IsBh predicate and the full Bose–Chowla conjecture for arbitrary $h \ge 2$, connecting to the resolved Sidon set case ($h = 2$, Problem #30).
keyInsights: The Bose–Chowla construction uses the map $t \mapsto t + t^3$ in $\mathbb{F}_{p^3}^*$ to produce B₃ sets of optimal size $\sim p \sim N^{1/3}$, exploiting that the cubing map is injective when $\gcd(3, p^3-1) = 1$

Green's upper bound $(7/2)^{1/3} N^{1/3}$ comes from bounding the additive energy $E_3(A)$ and applying moment inequalities—the factor 7/2 arises from counting ordered vs unordered representations of triple sums
The gap between constants 1 and 1.519 is fundamentally about whether algebraic constructions from finite fields are the densest possible, or whether non-algebraic constructions could do better

The B₃ problem sits at the threshold where Fourier-analytic methods (effective for B₂/Sidon sets) become insufficient: the lack of a B₃ analogue of the Erdős–Turán $N^{1/2} + O(N^{1/4})$ bound reflects deeper structural obstacles

The formalization distinguishes between the ordered-triple definition (used here, closer to the counting argument) and the multiset definition (equivalent but harder to formalize), a meaningful design choice for the Lean representation

sections.title: B₃ Sets
sections.summary: Defines threeSums (the image of ordered triples under addition) and IsB3 (injectivity of the sum map on ordered triples from A). The definition requires $a_1 + b_1 + c_1 = a_2 + b_2 + c_2$ with ordering constraints to imply equality of triples.

sections.title: Maximum B₃ Subset Size
sections.summary: Defines maxB3Size N as the supremum of cardinalities of B₃ subsets of {1,...,N}, using Finset.powerset and filter over the B₃ predicate. This is the extremal function $f(N)$ central to the problem.

sections.title: The Conjecture
sections.summary: States ErdosProblem241: for all $\varepsilon > 0$, eventually $(1-\varepsilon)N^{1/3} \le f(N) \le (1+\varepsilon)N^{1/3}$. This $\varepsilon$-$N_0$ formulation captures $f(N) \sim N^{1/3}$ precisely.

sections.title: The Bose–Chowla Lower Bound
sections.summary: Axiomatizes the 1962 lower bound: $f(N) \ge (1-\varepsilon)N^{1/3}$ for all $N \ge N_0(\varepsilon)$. This is one half of the conjecture and is known to be true via explicit finite field constructions.

sections.title: Green's Upper Bound
sections.summary: Axiomatizes Green's 2001 result: $f(N) \le ((7/2)^{1/3}+\varepsilon)N^{1/3}$ for large $N$. The constant $(7/2)^{1/3} \approx 1.519$ is the best known and the gap to 1 is the open problem.

sections.title: Generalized Bₕ Sets
sections.summary: Defines IsBh for arbitrary $h \ge 2$ (using subset-sum injectivity), maxBhSize, and the general Bose–Chowla conjecture $f_h(N) \sim N^{1/h}$. Notes $h=2$ (Sidon sets) is resolved and the lower bound holds for all $h$.

sections.title: Known Small B₃ Sets
sections.summary: Axiomatizes that {1,2,4,8} is B₃ and states the trivial counting upper bound $k(k+1)(k+2) \le 18N$ from fitting $\binom{k+2}{3}$ distinct sums into the interval $[3, 3N]$.

conclusion.summary: This formalization captures the full structure of Erdős Problem 241: the B₃ set definition, the extremal function f(N), the precise asymptotic conjecture, both the Bose–Chowla lower bound and Green's upper bound, and the natural generalization to Bₕ sequences. The $100 prize problem reduces to closing the gap between upper bound constant $(7/2)^{1/3} \approx 1.519$ and the conjectured value of 1.
conclusion.implications:
**Theoretical Significance**: **Additive Combinatorics**: Resolution would determine whether algebraic (finite field) constructions are optimal among all B₃ sets, a question at the heart of the polynomial method in combinatorics. **Coding Theory**: B₃ sets are equivalent to certain constant-weight codes with restricted Hamming distances; the answer determines fundamental limits of such codes.

**General Bₕ Conjecture**: Progress on B₃ would likely inform techniques for all $h \ge 3$, where the gap between Bose–Chowla lower bounds and best upper bounds persists. **Fourier Analysis**: New upper bound techniques would likely require advances beyond current additive energy methods, potentially developing higher-order Fourier analysis for $B_h$ problems.
openQuestions: Can the upper bound constant for B₃ sets be reduced below $(7/2)^{1/3} \approx 1.519$?
Does $\lim_{N \to \infty} f(N)/N^{1/3}$ exist, or do the limsup and liminf differ?
Is there a non-algebraic B₃ construction that exceeds the Bose–Chowla density?
Can higher-order Fourier analysis (degree $\ge 2$ uniformity norms) improve B₃ upper bounds, analogously to how classical Fourier analysis works for B₂?

crossReferences.description: Problem #30 (Sidon sets) is the h=2 case of the Bₕ hierarchy. The Bose–Chowla conjecture for h=2 is essentially resolved, while h=3 (this problem) remains wide open.
Problem #153 studies gap variance in Sidon sumsets (A+A for Sidon A). Both problems concern the fine structure of sumsets from sets with restricted additive properties.
Problem #840 studies quasi-Sidon sets (relaxed B₂ condition). The B₃ problem similarly asks about the extremal size under additive uniqueness constraints, but for triples instead of pairs.
